title: The Week Capitec Listed, Days After Saambou Bank Collapsed
conflicts: Listing date: Forbes Africa and Profile's Stock Exchange Handbook give 18 February 2002; Stellenbosch Visio prints 18 September 2002 while also saying nine days after Saambou's collapse, so treated as a misprint. Share price: Visio gives expected R3, opening R2.75, low 80 cents; Business Day's standfirst says the bank was launched 'at R2 a share'; the story uses Visio's figures. Founding date: incorporation 1999, bank registration 2001 (Profile: 29 June 2001 as controlling company; Wikipedia: 1 March 2001); story says opened in 2001. Wikipedia names Jannie Mouton as a third founder; story credits PSG's backing.
notes: Correction to the slate: Le Roux was the first CEO (to 2004) and Stassen his successor (2004-2013). The 40% rate cut and cash shortfall are undated in Le Roux's account ('during the founding phases'), so the story does not date them. Quote stance is 'challenges' (Ben Sira on helping the poor without waiting, set against lending at a return). News24, BusinessTech, Daily Investor and Capitec's own site could not be read.
